name: 02-web-server
description:
A web server in a container, published on the Docker host: what *port mapping* does.

**web** runs BusyBox httpd on port 80. Its port mapping publishes it as port **8080** of the Docker host.

## Try it
1. **Deploy**. Click **web**: under *Port mappings*, the link opens `http://<Docker host>:8080` in your browser.
2. In web's **Console**, look at the server and its page:
   ```
   ss -tlnp
   cat /var/www/index.html
   curl -v http://localhost/
   ```
3. Change the page, then reload it in the browser:
   ```
   vi /var/www/index.html
   ```
4. On the Docker host (**Console** in the Docker Host pane), see how Docker publishes the port:
   ```
   docker ps --format '{{.Names}}  {{.Ports}}'
   sudo iptables -t nat -L DOCKER -n
   ```

> [!TIP]
> The page is rewritten by web's startup commands every time it starts. Edit the startup commands (click **web**) to change it for good.

## Questions
- [ ] The server listens on port 80. Why does the browser use 8080?
- [ ] Two containers can both listen on port 80. Can both be published as 8080? Why?
- [ ] What happens to your edit after *Stop all* and *Start all*? Why?

nodes.name: web
nodes.startup:
# The web page cat > /var/www/index.html < $(hostname)

Hello from $(hostname)

This page is served by BusyBox httpd in a container, published as port 8080 of the Docker host.

HTML # The web server: BusyBox httpd on port 80, serving /var/www pkill -x httpd 2>/dev/null; busybox-extras httpd -p 80 -h /var/www

images.dockerlab/web:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# A small web server (BusyBox httpd), plus the end-host tools: full ip, packet capture, DNS lookups, web requests
RUN apk add --no-cache busybox-extras iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils
RUN mkdir -p /var/www
